articles.title: CSL, NeST Unveil India First Hybrid Laser Arc Welding Tech - The Open Press
articles.content: Technology CSL and NeST Unveil India's First Indigenous Hybrid Laser Arc Welding Technology Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL), in collaboration with SFO Technologies (NeST Group), has unveiled India's first indigenously designed and developed Hybrid Laser Arc Welding (HLAW) technology at the Ad… Published By : Technology Desk , Kochi Last Updated: November 15, 2026, 12:35 IST Officials at the unveiling of the hybrid laser arc welding system at the SFO Technologies facility in Kalamassery, Kochi. Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL), in collaboration with SFO Technologies (NeST Group), has unveiled India's first indigenously designed and developed Hybrid Laser Arc Welding (HLAW) technology at the Advanced Laser Engineering Centre and HLAW R and D Facility in Kalamassery. The unveiling marks a step forward for the country's growing capabilities in advanced manufacturing. The indigenous system integrates a 12 kW fibre laser, a six-axis industrial robot and MIG welding technology, achieving welding speeds of up to 2 metres per minute. The system was jointly developed to address real-world shipbuilding requirements, and the innovation has significant potential for automated ship panel fabrication, with applications extending to defence, railways, energy and heavy engineering. A public-private push for self-reliance The project has been described as a powerful example of public-private partnership driving indigenous innovation, advanced manufacturing and India's technological self-reliance. By combining laser and arc welding with robotics, the technology is expected to speed up shipbuilding and cut dependence on imported welding systems. Hybrid laser arc welding brings together the deep penetration of a laser with the gap-bridging ability of arc welding, making it suited to the thick steel panels used in ships. For Indian shipyards, an indigenous system of this kind means faster fabrication lines and less reliance on foreign equipment suppliers. Frequently Asked Questions What is hybrid laser arc welding? Hybrid laser arc welding combines a laser beam with conventional arc welding in a single process. It pairs the deep penetration of the laser with the arc's ability to bridge gaps, making it suited to thick steel panels. Who developed India's first indigenous HLAW technology? Cochin Shipyard Limited developed it in collaboration with SFO Technologies of the NeST Group, at the Advanced Laser Engineering Centre and HLAW R and D Facility in Kalamassery. How fast can the system weld? The system achieves welding speeds of up to 2 metres per minute, using a 12 kW fibre laser, a six-axis industrial robot and MIG welding technology. Where will the technology be used? It has significant potential for automated ship panel fabrication, with applications extending to defence, railways, energy and heavy engineering. articles.title: NIBE Successfully Tests Made-in-India SURyaSTRA Universal Rocket Launcher up to 300 ...
articles.content: On November 11, 2026, Pune-based private defence manufacturer NIBE Limited successfully executed fresh firing trials for SURyaSTRA, which is India’s first domestically produced Universal Rocket Launcher System (URLS). The comprehensive evaluations were conducted at the Integrated Test Range (ITR) in Chandipur, Odisha. During the live-fire tests, the indigenous system thoroughly validated its versatility by engaging targets across four distinct distance brackets: 30 km, 50 km, 150 km, and its maximum striking range of 300 km. Technical specifications reveal that the platform delivers exceptional accuracy with a Circular Error Probable (CEP) of less than five metres, ensuring highly precise surface-to-surface strikes. The foundation of SURyaSTRA stems from a major technology collaboration agreement signed in July 2025 between NIBE Limited and Israel’s Elbit Systems. By integrating Elbit's Precise & Universal Launching System (PULS) architecture with India's domestic manufacturing framework, the companies created a modular launcher capable of firing multiple ammunition sizes, including 122mm, 160mm, and 306mm rockets. This modular engineering provides immense operational flexibility for the armed forces. Because the platform can be mounted on heavy-duty carriers like the BEML High Mobility Vehicle (HMV), it allows troops to execute rapid "shoot-and-scoot" manoeuvres. More importantly, military units can seamlessly switch between different rocket calibres for various mission profiles on a single vehicle, removing the heavy logistical burden of maintaining entirely separate launcher variants for different engagement distances. The latest successful demonstrations in Odisha follow a crucial ₹293-crore purchase order granted to NIBE Limited by the Indian Army in January 2026. Authorised under the government's emergency procurement programme, the rapid development and validation of the SURyaSTRA system represent a massive triumph for the 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' vision, significantly reducing the nation's reliance on imported artillery and boosting India's self-reliance in the defence sector. articles.title: Mysuru Gets India's First 8K LED Dome Planetarium Where You Can Explore The Universe
articles.content: Home / India / Travel / Mysuru Gets India’s First 8K LED Dome Planetarium Where You Can Explore The Universe Mysuru is now home to India's first 8K-resolution LED Dome Planetarium, COSMOS-Mysuru, featuring a 15-metre tilted dome, over 4.2 crore LEDs and immersive astronomy experiences. by Tashika Tyagi Updated: November 15, 2026 11:56 AM Share Cover Image Courtesy: Instagram/narendramodi If exploring space, watching galaxies come alive and getting a closer look at the universe sounds exciting, Mysuru has a new attraction worth adding to your travel bucket list. Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium recently, marking the launch of India’s first 8K-resolution LED Dome Planetarium. Located on the University of Mysore campus at the foothills of Chamundi Hills, the facility promises an immersive experience for astronomy enthusiasts, students and curious travellers. COSMOS-Mysuru : India’s First 8K LED Dome Planetarium According to India Today, unlike conventional planetariums that use projectors to cast images onto a dome, COSMOS-Mysuru uses LED panels to display visuals directly on its curved surface. Think of it as one giant, immersive screen that surrounds the audience with images of stars, planets and galaxies. The planetarium features a 15-metre-wide tilted dome comprising approximately 6,150 LED panels and over 4.27 crore individual LEDs. The dome is tilted at an angle of 15 degrees, adding to the immersive viewing experience. Its 8K-resolution technology promises sharper visuals, better contrast and deeper blacks, allowing visitors to explore astronomical phenomena in remarkable detail. Another interesting feature is its ability to support real-time astronomical visualisations. Powered by 14 master computers, the system can run space simulations, zoom into celestial data and even adapt presentations based on audience questions. This makes the experience more interactive than simply watching a pre-recorded space film. Also Read: PM Modi To Unveil ₹15,600 Cr Projects In Bengaluru & Flag Off New Vande Bharat Express More Than Just A Planetarium, It’s An Astronomy Learning Centre COSMOS-Mysuru is not just about giving visitors a closer look at space. Developed by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics in collaboration with the University of Mysore , the facility is also envisioned as a centre for astronomy education, research and training. The Sky Theatre can accommodate approximately 150 to 168 visitors, with shows and outreach activities planned in Kannada, English and Hindi. The facility will also support student training, data-analysis programmes and educational workshops. For those planning a visit, regular public screenings and ticket bookings are expected to begin after the final calibration and testing are completed. Once fully operational, the planetarium plans to host two to three public 8K shows daily, while morning slots will be reserved for school and college groups. Ticket prices and booking details are expected to be announced through the official COSMOS portal. Also Read: Mysuru Has A Pet-Friendly Hotel Ft. Bird-Inspired Cocktails, Rooftop Pool & Cosy Rooms With this new addition, Mysuru has another interesting attraction for travellers, especially families looking to combine sightseeing with a little science and learning. articles.title: India's First LED Dome Planetarium Opens in Mysuru With COSMOS Attraction | Outlook Traveller
articles.content: India's First LED Dome Planetarium Opens In Mysuru With COSMOS Attraction India's first LED dome planetarium opens in Mysuru, offering visitors an immersive journey through astronomy, space science and the wonders of the universe By Tenzin Chodon Updated on: 15 Nov 2026, 10:00 am India's first LED dome planetarium opens in Mysuru : Instagram/@narendramodi Mysuru has added a new attraction to its educational and cultural landscape with the inauguration of COSMOS Planetarium at the University of Mysore campus, near the foothills of Chamundi Hills. India's first LED dome planetarium, the state-of-the-art facility aims to introduce visitors to the wonders of astronomy and offer an immersive experience of the universe. Inaugurated on November 13, the planetarium is expected to provide students, researchers and astronomy enthusiasts with opportunities to explore celestial bodies, planets and other astronomical phenomena. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who inaugurated the facility, said COSMOS would encourage young minds to develop scientific curiosity and pursue new discoveries. India's First LED Dome Planetarium Located on the University of Mysore campus, COSMOS Planetarium features advanced LED dome technology that offers visitors an immersive view of the universe. The facility is designed to make complex scientific concepts easier to understand while encouraging interest in space science and astronomy . Describing it as an extraordinary experience, Modi congratulated the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, the University of Mysore, various government departments and everyone associated with the project. He also called for greater participation by school and college students, urging the planetarium's management to coordinate with educational institutions and organise visits. Mysuru's Legacy Of Science And Learning The new planetarium offers an immersive journey through the universe Photo: Instagram/@narendramodi The new planetarium offers an immersive journey through the universe Photo: Instagram/@narendramodi The new planetarium also adds to Mysuru's long association with education and scientific research. The University of Mysore was established during the reign of Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar, while the Mysuru royal family played an important role in laying the foundation for the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) in Bengaluru. During the inauguration, Modi drew a parallel between COSMOS and Viveka Smaraka, another institution he had recently inaugurated in the city. While the memorial encourages visitors to look within and explore spiritual knowledge, the planetarium invites them to look towards the skies and understand the mysteries of the universe. He also highlighted the contributions of ancient Indian astronomers such as Aryabhata, Varahamihira, Bhaskaracharya and Neelakantha Somayaji, who made significant observations and carried out complex mathematical calculations despite not having access to modern instruments. Follow our WhatsApp channel India's Growing Achievements In Space Research The inauguration also highlighted India's growing presence in space exploration. Among the major milestones are Chandrayaan-3 , which made India the first country to achieve a soft landing near the Moon's south polar region, and Aditya-L1, the country's first space-based solar observatory. India has also become the fourth country in the world to demonstrate space docking and undocking capabilities. articles.title: AIIMS Delhi Performs India's First Fetal Spinal Cord Surgery - Urban Acres
articles.content: Home Breaking News AIIMS Delhi Performs India’s First Fetal Spinal Cord Surgery Breaking News AIIMS Delhi Performs India’s First Fetal Spinal Cord Surgery By Ananya Sharma November 14, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp AIIMS Delhi doctors have performed India’s first reported open fetal spinal cord surgery, operating on a 25-week-old foetus with myelomeningocele, a serious congenital defect in which part of the spinal cord and its protective membranes protrude through an opening in the spine. The six-hour procedure was carried out on 12 November at the Neurosciences Centre, according to AIIMS. More than 30 doctors, nurses and other healthcare workers from multiple specialties were involved in the operation, which aimed to limit continuing damage to exposed nerve tissue before birth. Myelomeningocele can cause paralysis of the legs, difficulty in movement and hydrocephalus, a condition in which excess fluid accumulates in the brain. The usual treatment is surgery after birth, but nerve damage may already have occurred by then. AIIMS said the fetal procedure was intended to reduce that ongoing exposure and improve some outcomes after delivery. The operation was led by Professor Deepak Gupta of the neurosurgery department. Professor Neena Malhotra and Professor K. Aparna Sharma managed maternal-fetal medicine and obstetric care. Anaesthesia responsibilities were handled by teams led by Professor Vimi Revery, Professor Rashmi Ramachandra, Professor Mihir Prakash Pandia and Professor Gyanendra Pal Singh. Specialists from radiodiagnosis, plastic surgery, paediatrics, obstetrics and gynaecology, along with nursing staff, also participated. The preparation took more than five weeks and included detailed fetal examinations, ultrasound and other imaging, counselling for the mother about the illness and surgical risks, anaesthesia planning and practice sessions. AIIMS said the surgery was conducted using high-capacity microscopy and continuous ultrasound guidance. The institution said the treatment was provided free of cost under the central government’s Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram scheme. The mother and foetus will continue to be monitored throughout the pregnancy, delivery and the newborn period. The procedure is not a complete cure for myelomeningocele. AIIMS said the child will require continued specialist follow-up. The international Management of Myelomeningocele Study, cited in the report, found that 40% of children who underwent fetal surgery required a shunt to drain excess brain fluid by 12 months of age, compared with 82% of those who had surgery after birth. The study also reported some improved motor outcomes and a lower incidence of Chiari II-related displacement of the lower part of the brain. However, fetal surgery carries risks, including premature delivery and complications linked to the surgical scar on the uterus. For that reason, the procedure is generally reserved for selected cases at specialist centres with the required maternal-fetal, neurosurgical, anaesthesia, imaging and neonatal capabilities. The case also highlights the importance of prevention and early monitoring. The neural tube develops and closes by about 28 days after conception, often before a pregnancy is detected. Doctors therefore advise folic acid intake before conception, appropriate folate fortification of food and stronger monitoring of data related to neural tube defects....
